scope: Independent read-only review of the offline checker source, recorded synthetic self-test, root review, and normative hardware-evidence documentation. No tests rerun and no hardware evidence created.

behavior_review.calibration: Requires explicit positive rational tick rate, named clock, kind, calibration file hash, and matching clock/rate/kind values in the calibration artifact. Verifies file consistency, not physical calibration accuracy or uncertainty.
behavior_review.counter_contract: Requires explicit width 1-64, wrap_count, raw tick in range, one declared reset epoch shared by all timestamps, and explicit single-epoch/reset and wrap policies; absolute ticks use wrap_count * 2^width + tick.
behavior_review.provenance: Requires nonempty artifact pins and verifies each file hash. A matching pin proves only which supplied bytes were read, not that they came from a device or a complete capture.
behavior_review.windows_and_frames: Checks ordered nonoverlapping exact 60 s then 600 s windows, fixed floor-30-Hz release schedule, distinct IDs and intended source/publication/display identity, timestamps and increasing display order, flags, supplied content-hash equality, queue bounds, per-frame underruns, and supplied whole-window health totals.
behavior_review.strict_latency: Uses integer rational comparison 100 * latency_ticks * rate_denominator < rate_numerator for every packet-complete to validated-publication sample. Exactly 10 ms fails regardless of median/percentile.
behavior_review.offline_flags: hardware_execution_verified and hardware_acceptance remain false in all results, including a numerical pass labelled hardware_capture.

limits: Queue peaks, health totals, calibration metadata, event flags, and provenance are supplied trace observations/claims; offline hash and consistency checks cannot attest device execution, unlogged events, or that supplied health totals cover real operation.

A synthetic or hardware-labeled fixture can pass numerical checks but cannot qualify hardware. Independent capture provenance, calibrated device counters, real contention, and complete production integration remain required.
The self-test demonstrates checker behavior against synthetic fixtures only; it is not a hardware, simulation, or product performance result.
